categories.title: Daily stand-up

phrases.text: Yesterday I shipped the X endpoint and fixed a flaky test in Y.
Today I am picking up the Z ticket; I expect to open a PR by the end of the day.
The only thing blocking me is waiting for a review on the W MR.
I will be on support rotation this afternoon, so progress may be slower.

prompts: Give a stand-up update: what did you do yesterday, what will you do today, and what is blocking you?

categories.title: Code review comments

phrases.text: Could we extract this into a helper? It would make the flow easier to follow.
This looks correct, but I would add a test for the timeout branch.
Nit: the variable name is a bit vague; maybe deadline or budget would be clearer.
Good catch on the race condition. Let's document why we need the lock here.

prompts: Give feedback on a pull request that works but is hard to read. Be kind and specific.

categories.title: Explaining an incident

phrases.text: The symptom was intermittent 502s on the offers list starting at 14:00 UTC.
The root cause was a downstream call without its own deadline, which ate the caller's budget.
We mitigated by shortening the timeout and letting the best-effort enrichment fail open.
The follow-up is to add per-endpoint p99.9 alerts and a circuit breaker.

prompts: Describe a production incident you investigated: the symptom, the root cause, and the fix.

categories.title: Architecture overview

phrases.text: The service owns the listing lifecycle and publishes events to Kafka when the state changes.
Reads go through a cache; writes hit PostgreSQL and then invalidate the cache.
The main failure modes are stale cache, partition lag, and downstream unavailability.
We chose synchronous calls for launch speed, with a plan to move to an event-driven sync.

prompts: Describe the architecture of a service you know well: what it does, what it talks to, and where it can fail.

categories.title: Behavioral interview

phrases.text: I am a backend engineer with three years of Go, mostly in marketplace and scoring systems.
The situation was that return orders had stopped being saved for 24 days.
My task was to find the cause, stop the loss, and recover the data the same day.
I traced it through git history and logs, shipped a tolerant parser, and replayed 10,394 records.
The result was full recovery in about two hours and new alerts on zero business throughput.

prompts: Tell me about yourself, as at the start of a job interview.
Describe a production incident you led from detection to resolution.
Tell me about a time you had to ship something fast with limited people.
Describe the hardest technical problem you have solved and what you learned from it.
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague. What happened and how did it end?
Explain a trade-off you made recently: what you chose, what you gave up, and why.
Tell me about a mistake you made at work and how you handled it.
